titre: At the first Oscars, the winners were known three months in advance
accroche: The first ceremony, on May 16, 1929, lasts only fifteen minutes in front of 270 people. The winners were announced three months earlier.
contenu_vulgarise:
On May 16, 1929, 270 people dine at the Roosevelt Hotel in Hollywood. Douglas Fairbanks, president of the Academy, hands out twelve awards, including the first prize for best picture. Members can bring guests for five dollars. The ceremony itself lasts only fifteen minutes, according to Wikipedia, and is broadcast neither on radio nor on television.

The winners are known in advance: the ceremony takes place, the Academy itself states, three months after the results were announced. Emil Jannings, notified of his best actor award, even had time to be photographed with the statuette before leaving for Germany.

## A $500 statuette, two supreme awards

The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences is only two years old: it was founded in 1927 by Louis B. Mayer to bring together the five branches of the profession. Its statuette was designed in 1928 by Cedric Gibbons, MGM's art director, and the sculptor George Stanley received $500 to execute it.

The rules differ greatly from today's. An award can honor a single work, several, or a whole year: Janet Gaynor is named best actress for three films, 7th Heaven, Street Angel, and Sunrise. There are two directing awards, one for drama (Frank Borzage), the other for comedy (Lewis Milestone). And there are two supreme awards: best picture, which goes to Wings, a silent film, and “unique and artistic” production, which goes to Sunrise. The Academy later recognizes the first as the higher one, and drops the second.

## Not all the winners are films

Two special awards show how unsettled the era is. Charlie Chaplin receives one for The Circus, in which he is actor, writer, director, and producer all at once. Warner Bros. receives one for producing *The Jazz Singer*, presented as the pioneering talking picture, which “revolutionized the industry.” The film that upends Hollywood in 1927 thus receives a special award.

What the first ceremony reveals is an institution still looking for its form: a trade dinner, without broadcast, where sometimes a film is honored and sometimes the whole body of a year's work. The suspense one thinks inseparable from the Oscars was not yet part of them.

quiz.question: What most sets the first Oscars ceremony (1929) apart from today's?
choix: The winners were announced three months before the ceremony, which was not broadcast
The ceremony was broadcast on radio, a first for a film event
The ceremony was held in a large theater and lasted more than three hours
Each award honored a single film, as today
quiz.explication: The results had been public for three months, and the ceremony, a dinner for 270 people, lasted only fifteen minutes. It was broadcast neither on radio nor on television, and an award could honor several films: Janet Gaynor is honored for three films at once.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Why does Charlie Chaplin receive a special award for The Circus in 1929?
choix: Because he is actor, writer, director, and producer all at once in it
Because the film broke all the box office records of 1928
Because the Academy wanted to honor his entire silent career
Because the film had been rejected in all the competitive categories
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text specifies that Chaplin receives a special award for The Circus because he is actor, writer, director, and producer all at once in it, with no mention of a box office record or a career award.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Why does Janet Gaynor win the best actress award in 1929?
choix: For a single role in Sunrise, judged the most striking of the year
For the three films taken together, 7th Heaven, Street Angel, and Sunrise
For her performance in Wings, alongside Clara Bow
For dubbing a supporting role in The Jazz Singer
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text states that Janet Gaynor is named best actress for the three films taken together, 7th Heaven, Street Angel, and Sunrise, and not for a single role.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What distinguishes the best picture award in 1929?
choix: Only one award was given, shared equally between Wings and Sunrise
The award was granted only after a second vote, a month later
Two supreme awards existed then: Wings and Sunrise each receive one
The best picture award was taken back from Wings a few months after the ceremony
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text explains that there were then two supreme awards, best picture for Wings and unique and artistic production for Sunrise, with the Academy later dropping the second.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What could Emil Jannings do before leaving for Germany, in 1929?
choix: Publicly refuse his statuette, finding the ceremony not solemn enough for his taste
Deliver a long acceptance speech broadcast live on national radio
Present the best picture award himself to the Wings team in front of the audience
Be photographed with his best actor statuette, already notified of his award
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text reports that Emil Jannings, notified of his best actor award, had had time to be photographed with the statuette before leaving for Germany.
